question: FABLE-C4 established that 46 of 70 generically source-blocked families are held after all. Five attached. What stands between the repository and the other forty-one, exactly?
answer: Two bounded populations and nothing else. Neither is a search: every artifact below is already named, already located, and already carries a recorded SHA-256. One population needs a page opened; the other needs an index extended to bytes this container cannot currently see.

official-form:CXP Notice of Court Date for Motion

whatAlreadyAttached.whyTheseAndNotTheRest: The reconciler admits an identity established by reading the document itself, and refuses one established from a title, a filename or a revision date. That line is FABLE-C4's own; this file does not move it, it measures what it costs.

cohortA.name: ONE_DOCUMENT_READ_AWAY
cohortA.whatIsTrueOfThemAll: The bytes are held in the Master Library, the committed corpus index carries the exact path at the exact SHA-256, and FABLE-C4 established the identity from the corpus's recorded title or form number rather than from the document's own text.
cohortA.whatIsOwed: One read per artifact: open the held file, read the identity printed on page one, and record it as confirmed_from_document_text with the sentence it was read from. The reconciler then binds it with no further change — the tier already exists and the hash already matches.
cohortA.whyItIsNotDoneHere: Reading a PDF's printed identity requires the Master Library mounted (bash scripts/rcap-corpus/bootstrap-private-corpus.sh). A Captain integrating central state does not hold the corpus, and asserting an identity it has not read would be exactly the inference the tier refuses.

cohortB.whatIsOwed: Extend the committed corpus index to these custodies, hashing each file at index time rather than trusting the recorded hash. Once a path is in the index at its real hash, cohort A's rule and the existing tiers reach it unchanged.

readAndRefused.whatIsTrueOfThemAll: Somebody opened the document and what it said did not establish the identity the family names. These are finished reads, not owed ones.
readAndRefused.whatIsOwed: A determination, not another read. Each entry's readOutcome names the question: one census label over two held documents, a held document narrower than the label it is asked to serve, or a later revision than the family names.

Alabama carries three documents in the packs and all three were opened: C-10-CRIMINAL prints "Form C-10-CRIMINAL / AFFIDAVIT OF SUBSTANTIAL HARDSHIP AND ORDER", C-94A prints "Form C-94A Rev. 10/2023 / PETITION FOR ORDER OF LIMITED RELIEF" and recites Act 2019-464 rather than the expungement act, and SBI-FORM-46 is the ALEA criminal-history review application. artifactList.officialTitle: (no such document) — "ACIC Uniform Petition to Seal" / "ACIC Uniform Order to Seal"
artifactList.readOutcome: Read and refused: the label names no document, and two families need different ones. A case-insensitive text search for "uniform" across all twenty-two Arkansas files in the D packs returns nothing — the word is printed on none of them. What ACIC actually publishes is an act-specific and offence-class-specific pair, and both members of the pair print their own scope on page 1: "PETITION TO SEAL FELONY UNDER ACT 1460 OF 2013; A.C.A.16-90-1401, Et. Seq." and "ORDER TO SEAL MISDEMEANORS UNDER ACT 1460 OF 2013; A.C.A.16-90-1401, Et. Seq." The reconciler binds a label globally, so a single binding of ACIC-UNIFORM-PETITION-TO-SEAL would hand the felony petition to ar-misdemeanor-seal-set or the misdemeanor order to ar-felony-seal-set. That is a determination for the owner — split the label per family, or model the pair by act and offence class — and not a binding.

artifactList.officialTitle: Petition to Seal Misdemeanors under Act 1460 of 2013 (A.C.A. § 16-90-1401 et seq.)
artifactList.readOutcome: Not held after all, and the D packs do not change that. Arkansas appears 44 times in the committed corpus index — 22 entries under master_library and the same 22 form numbers under d_source_packs — so the packs added no Arkansas document the Master Library did not already have. The only misdemeanor petition in either custody is offence-specific: its page 1 reads "PETITION TO SEAL A MISDEMEANOR CONVICTION FOR DRIVING OR BOATING WHILE INTOXICATED" and paragraph 1 recites "Driving or Boating While Intoxicated in violation of Ark. Code Ann. §5-65-103". The general Act 1460 misdemeanor petition is held nowhere, exactly as the earlier lane found; the matching ORDER to seal misdemeanors under Act 1460 IS held, which is what makes the absence easy to misread.

artifactList.readOutcome: Not held. Every Utah expungement form in the packs was opened and each prints its own approved number in its page footer: "1000EXF Approved, April 11, 2022 / Petition to Expunge Records with Certificate of Eligibility", "1002EXF Approved April 11, 2022 / Petition to Expunge Records – Traffic Charge", "1003EXF Approved March 9, 2020 / Petition to Expunge Records – Cannabis Conviction", "1020EXF Approved, April 11, 2022 / Order on Petition to Expunge Records with Certificate of Eligibility" and "1022EXF Approved April 11, / Order on Petition to Expunge Records – Traffic Conviction". 1023EX is not among them (the held Utah orders print 1020EXF and 1022EXF in their own footers); binding a neighbouring number would hand a participant the wrong pleading.

whatThisDoesNotEstablish: No family is promoted, and no family's state changes because this file exists.
An artifact appearing here is not proof the family that names it will build; it is proof that its source is located and what remains to be done about it.

FABLE-C3 established that 37 source obligations across this territory are held live by other lanes, and that no packet-build grant exists for any of the 67 families it read. Attaching a source does not mint a grant.
